result.summary: Replaces the BCC eBPF test consumer in USDT functional tests with GDB. Nodes run as debugger child processes that enable USDT tracepoints and inspect arguments directly upon execution. This eliminates dependencies on BCC, matching host kernel headers, and privileged CI containers, deleting roughly 660 lines of test harness and CI code.
result.problem: Running USDT functional tests currently requires BCC, matching kernel headers, and elevated BPF execution privileges. This makes tracepoint tests awkward for developers to execute locally and forces CI to run in a privileged container.
evidence: Author description: 'The USDT functional tests currently use BCC to attach eBPF programs to Bitcoin Core’s tracepoints. This requires BCC, matching kernel headers, and elevated BPF permissions, making the tests awkward to run locally and requiring a privileged container in CI.'

Author description: 'All five tests can run with GDB and binutils, without BCC or matching kernel headers. The ASan CI job no longer needs a privileged container and uses SYS_PTRACE instead... Overall, the change removes roughly 660 lines of test and CI code.'
result.scope_notes: Modifies test harness scripts and CI workflow definitions only. The author explicitly notes that the change stops testing consumer-side eBPF compilation/delivery paths and requires disabling LeakSanitizer for traced nodes because it cannot run under ptrace.
result.card: This PR replaces the BCC and eBPF consumer framework in USDT functional tests with GDB. Running USDT tests previously required BCC, matching host kernel headers, and elevated BPF privileges, which made local execution difficult and required a privileged container in CI. By inspecting probe arguments via GDB as a child process, the tests verify Bitcoin Core probe metadata, triggers, and values using standard tools while deleting roughly 660 lines of embedded BPF and CI code. The trade-off is that consumer-side kernel BPF execution paths are no longer exercised and LeakSanitizer is disabled for traced processes under ptrace.
uncertainties: The full diff was not provided, though the description and commit messages detail the implementation clearly.

risk.why: Touches only functional test infrastructure and CI setup; a mistake could only break USDT test execution or fail to catch tracepoint regressions.
